stem.en: A ridge of loose rock lies right across a valley, long after the ice has gone. What does it tell us?

text.en: It is a lateral moraine, showing where two glaciers joined.

feedback.en: Lateral moraines lie along the sides. A ridge across a valley is at the end of the ice.

text.en: It is a medial moraine, showing the middle of the glacier.

feedback.en: A medial moraine runs down the middle, not across the valley.

text.en: It is a sand dune, showing the wind direction.

feedback.en: Dunes are sand shaped by wind, not till left by ice.

text.en: It is a terminal moraine, showing how far the ice reached.

feedback.en: Right. It marks the furthest advance of the glacier.

explanation.en: A terminal moraine forms at the end of a glacier and lies across the valley. It marks the furthest advance of the ice, and it stays after the ice has melted.

hints.en: Which part of a glacier lies across the valley?
